title: American: THE Premier Global Airline Based in the U.S.
summary_zh: 本期节目围绕美国航空（AA）首席商务官Nat Pieper提出的最新战略愿景——成为“总部位于美国的头号高端全球航司”展开深度剖析。Brian与Brett一致认可美航告别单纯成本控制、转向高端产品投资（如全舱座椅屏幕加装及即将公布的全新宽体机订单）的必要性，并反驳了美联航CEO关于市场仅容得下两家高端航司的论断。然而，针对重建洛杉矶（LAX）跨太平洋门户以补齐全球化短板的计划，两人产生激烈交锋：Brett结合本地O&D数据指出LAX格局高度分散，是美航布局亚太的“最不坏选择”；Brian则警告此举无异于“企业自杀”，认为美航不仅曾在LAX亚洲航线巨亏，更将招致盈利丰厚的达美与美联航发动针对性的运力与价格绞杀。
key_takeaways_zh: 美国航空确立向高端化与全球化转型的战略北极星，彻底摒弃过去依赖控制成本、容忍产品劣势的经营逻辑。
美航正推进客舱全面升级并计划在两个月内敲定高两舱配比的全新宽体机订单，但受限于储备订单积压，运力红利需等到2030年代才能释放。
旅客为高端舱位付费已成为不可逆的长期趋势，美国市场完全有空间容纳达美与美联航之外的更多高端航司共存。
美航计划重返洛杉矶（LAX）重建跨太平洋门户以争夺核心市场联名信用卡消费，但在亚洲航司云集、本地O&D极度分散的LAX，没有任何航司能真正实现垄断。
面对达美完善的LAX航站楼基建优势以及美联航随时可能发起的宽体机针对性价格战，美航重押LAX亚太市场面临巨额亏损的极高风险。

highlights.title_zh: 美航确立高端全球航司新愿景
highlights.summary_zh: Brett透露美航首席商务官Nat Pieper明确提出了打造“美国头号高端全球航司”的单一愿景。Brian与Brett认为，尽管“头号”一词略显夸张，但这标志着美航终于告别过去单纯削减成本的拼凑式策略，向一线员工传递了以产品投入驱动收入增长的清晰方向。
highlights.quote_en: So Nat told me definitively that American has a vision.

highlights.title_zh: 资本开支边界与全新宽体机订单
highlights.summary_zh: 美航虽因资本开支限制排除了抄底引进巴航工业E2小机型机队的可能，但在高端化硬件上毫不吝啬。除推进耗时费力的客舱座椅屏幕加装与现有宽体机改装外，美航预计将在未来两个月内宣布一笔高两舱配比的全新宽体机订单。
highlights.quote_en: There is a new widebody order coming. He told me it would be within the next two months.

highlights.title_zh: 反驳市场仅容两家高端航司论断
highlights.summary_zh: 针对美联航CEO Scott Kirby宣称市场仅容得下两家高端航司的观点，两人认为这只是其引导华尔街预期的舆论策略。随着旅客青睐高端产品的十年长期趋势确立，美航与阿拉斯加航空顺应需求升级具备充分生存空间，真正的挑战在于改装与飞机交付的漫长周期。
highlights.quote_en: They're literally doing exactly what their customers tell them that they want.

highlights.title_zh: 重返LAX重建跨太平洋门户
highlights.summary_zh: 为兑现全球化愿景并在核心都市圈撬动联名信用卡消费，美航决定重点扩建洛杉矶（LAX），重启疫情期间关闭的跨太平洋门户。Brett指出，由于达拉斯枢纽亚太潜力有限且纽约、芝加哥难以突围，LAX成了美航不得不吞下培育期巨亏的战略选择。
highlights.quote_en: Clearly, Nat feels it is time for American to take another run at the crown by reopening this LAX Pacific gateway that it closed during the pandemic.

highlights.title_zh: 数据解析LAX分散的竞争格局
highlights.summary_zh: 2025年美国交通部本地O&D数据显示，LAX国内市场排名第一的达美份额仅为23.7%，美航与美联航均不足20%，没有任何航司占据绝对主导。在跨太平洋市场上，众多亚洲航司扎堆直飞导致票价承压，使LAX成为全美乃至全球竞争最激烈的机场。
highlights.quote_en: LAX is, I would say unquestionably, the most competitive airport, big airport, in the US, if not the world.

highlights.title_zh: 机位瓶颈与对手的价格绞杀风险
highlights.summary_zh: Brett指出达美已率先完成LAX第2、3航站楼重建并坐拥27个登机口与贵宾室集群，而美航与美联航均受制于机位瓶颈。Brian则强调达美与美联航凭借丰厚的系统利润，完全有能力挤出少量宽体机时刻发动针对性价格战来拖垮美航，直言美航此举无异于“企业自杀”。
highlights.quote_en: You don't have to win LAX. It's nice to win LAX. You just have to ruin American.

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: I'm Brian Sumers and I write The Airline Observer.
transcript.zh: 我是 Brian Sumers，我是《The Airline Observer》的作者。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And I'm Brett Snyder, author of Cranky Flier. You're listening to The Air Show, the podcast where we talk about what happens in the business of the sky, brought to you by the Alaska Hawaiian Airlines pilots.
transcript.zh: 我是 Brett Snyder，《Cranky Flier》的作者。您正在收听的是《The Air Show》，这是一档讨论民航商业内幕的播客，本节目由阿拉斯加航空与夏威夷航空的飞行员赞助呈现。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And this week's episode is also sponsored by SkyGo and Plusgrade. Brian, it's just you and me this week, and I want to talk about, I guess I'll call it an interesting lunch that I had with American's Chief Commercial Officer, Nat Pieper, last week when he was in town.
transcript.zh: 本周的节目同样由 SkyGo 和 Plusgrade 赞助支持。Brian，这周就咱俩。我想聊聊上周美航（American Airlines）首席商务官 Nat Pieper 来洛杉矶时，我和他吃的一顿……姑且称之为挺有意思的午餐。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: That sounds interesting, Brett. So what are we doing today? We'll do about 30 minutes on branded snacks, or maybe we can discuss how they came up with those brown seat covers? Or maybe the coffin-like business class seats? What are we doing today?
transcript.zh: 听起来挺有意思啊，Brett。那我们今天聊什么？花个三十分钟聊聊定制品牌小零食？还是讨论一下他们是怎么想出用那些棕色座椅套的？抑或是那些像棺材一样的商务舱座椅？今天聊什么？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Mostly, it was just talking about where they should put the logo inside of each airplane, so I think you'd love it. But no, what we're going to talk about here... So Nat told me definitively that American has a vision. Do you believe this?
transcript.zh: 大部分时间都在聊每架飞机客舱里的航徽到底该贴哪儿，我想你肯定爱听。不过说正经的，我们今天真正要聊的是……Nat 非常明确地告诉我，美航是有战略愿景的。你敢信？

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: What is that vision, Brett?
transcript.zh: 那个愿景是什么，Brett？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: It is to be, quote, "the premier global airline based in the US," end quote.
transcript.zh: 原话是成为——引述原话，“总部位于美国的全球首屈一指的航空公司”，引述完毕。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: That is interesting. We'll talk about that in a moment. But I'm still kind of angry about something you said earlier, Brett. I think you mocked me by saying, jokingly, I assume, that you spoke about the placement of the American logo on every airplane with Nat.
transcript.zh: 有点意思。我们待会儿就聊这个。但我对你刚才说的话还是有点耿耿于怀，Brett。我觉得你是在嘲讽我，居然说——我猜是开玩笑吧——你和 Nat 聊了美航航徽在每架飞机上的摆放位置。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Look, if an airline wants to be the premier global airline based in the United States, brand is a huge part of that. Let's just ask Delta how that all works, okay? A lot of these airlines are still pretty much the same. The logo does matter, and stop mocking me.
transcript.zh: 听着，如果一家航空公司想成为总部位于美国的首要全球航司，品牌塑造至关重要。去问问达美航空是怎么运作的就知道了，好吗？这些航司很多方面大同小异，航徽确实很重要，别再嘲笑我了。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: So salty today.
transcript.zh: 今天火气这么大啊。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Anyways, this plan that Nat outlined to you, it of course will take more than marketing. This sort of thing has to come from the top. So presumably, Brett, American gave you the big news that if they want to do this, the board is going to give Scott Kirby a billion dollars to come back, right?
transcript.zh: 不管怎么说，Nat 向你描绘的这个宏图，单靠市场营销肯定是搞不定的。这种战略变革必须自上而下推动。所以想必，Brett，美航是不是给了你个独家大新闻——董事会打算给 Scott Kirby 十个亿求他回巢？对吧？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Well, we're going to start with that quarter you have to put in the jar right now. No, I do not believe that is the case. I actually don't know where this came from.
transcript.zh: 好吧，你先往罚款罐里扔个硬币再说。不，我觉得完全不可能。我其实根本不知道这战略到底打哪儿冒出来的。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: I don't know if it was Nat who is leading this charge, or if the board came down from on high and said, "This is who we are now," or... I mean, I guess there's the unlikely chance that Robert pushed this forward, but he didn't do that before.
transcript.zh: 我不知道是 Nat 在挑头推进，还是董事会高层下达旨意说“这就是我们未来的定位”，还是……我猜也有极小的可能是 Robert 推动的，但他以前可从来没这么干过。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Brett, enough joking, okay? You've made a few jokes. There's none bigger than Robert pushing this from the top, okay?
transcript.zh: Brett，别开玩笑了行吗？你开过好几个玩笑了，但没有哪个比“Robert 在高层力推这个”更好笑了，好吗？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: My apologies, but it could be the board. We don't know the inner machinations, if you will.
transcript.zh: 抱歉抱歉，但也有可能是董事会的授意。内部权力运作的玄机，谁又说得准呢。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: We could go on and on about making fun of this, but we're a serious podcast. "The premier global airline based in the United States," you say. Maybe it's at least good for this airline to have a North Star at this point?
transcript.zh: 我们当然可以一直调侃下去，但我们毕竟是一档严肃的播客。“总部位于美国的首要全球航司”，照你这么说，美航眼下至少能有个指路明灯（北极星），总归是件好事吧？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Oh, you mean a Polaris?
transcript.zh: 噢，你是指“北极星（Polaris）”商务舱吗？

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Brett, it's always going to be Connoisseur Class to me. You know that.
transcript.zh: Brett，在我心里，它永远是头等舱时代的“鉴赏家舱（Connoisseur Class）”。这你是知道的。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Oh, I love those cradle seats. But, uh, I agree with this. This is the mandate. It is a singular vision, which when was the last time American had a singular vision?
transcript.zh: 噢，我超喜欢那种摇篮椅。但是，呃，我赞同这一点。这就是核心使命。这是一个极其专一的愿景，而 American 上一次拥有如此统一专一的愿景是什么时候？

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: We going to make this joke again? It was going for great, Brett.
transcript.zh: 我们又要讲这个老梗了吗？当年他们可是奔着「追求卓越」（Going for great）去的啊，Brett。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: I don't think that was a singular vision. I'm pretty sure that was a brand exercise.
transcript.zh: 我不觉得那算什么统一愿景，我敢肯定那纯粹是一场品牌公关包装。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Look, this is so interesting to me because we may spend much of the next 30 minutes making fun of what Nat told you. But the thing is, with one different word, this makes a lot of sense. So he told you that they wanted to be the premier global airline in the United States, right?
transcript.zh: 听着，这对我来说太有意思了，因为接下来的30分钟里，我们可能会花大把时间去嘲讽 Nat 对你说的那些话。但关键在于，只要换一个词，这一切就完全说得通了。他告诉你，他们想成为美国「那家独一无二」的顶级全球性航司，对吧？

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: It's the "the" that we're laughing at. If he just said we want to be "a" premier airline based in the United States, it makes perfect sense. We know this is where the industry is going, and we know American was late to this. Good on them.
transcript.zh: 我们嘲笑的正是那个定冠词“The”。如果他只是说想成为美国本土的「一家」顶级航司，那就完全合情合理了。我们心知肚明这才是行业的走向，也知道 American 在这方面起步太晚。能这么做也是件好事。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Listen, man, let's just break this down. Let's start with every word in here, right? I think the easy one to get rid of is "United States." They are based in the United States. We understand that. They're not trying to beat Emirates, good to know.
transcript.zh: 听着，伙计，咱们不妨来拆解一下。咱们挨个词分析，对吧？我觉得最容易滤掉的是“美国”。他们本就立足美国，这毫无疑问，他们也没打算去干翻阿联酋航空，这很好理解。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: But let's talk about the "the," right? It's good to have a stretch goal as a company, but is it too much of a stretch? I mean, if you're a frontline person, does this motivate you?
transcript.zh: 但咱们来聊聊那个“独一无二的”（The），对吧？一家公司设定一个具有挑战性的远大目标是好事，但这是不是有点好高骛远了？我的意思是，如果你是一名一线员工，这能激励你吗？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Because now you've got everyone trying to go in the same direction. Okay, we're the global premier airline. Does this motivate you to do that? Or does this make you think like, come on, this is a joke. Like, we're not even close to that. How is that even possible?
transcript.zh: 因为现在是要让所有人齐心协力朝同一个方向走。好吧，我们是“那家顶级全球性航司”。这真能激励大家去达成目标吗？还是会让大家觉得，得了吧，这简直是个笑话。我们现在连边都还没摸到，这怎么可能？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: I guess that's the question on whether this makes sense or not, if it's too much of a stretch.
transcript.zh: 我想这才是这个口号到底合不合理的关键所在，它是不是目标定得脱离实际了。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: I don't know if it motivates the frontline, but I do think it helps the frontline understand where the airline wants to go. I was kind of joked that the last motto of American Airlines, which was really hard to communicate to anybody who worked there, but I really felt was true, was, let's be, you know, 12% worse than United and Delta on product, but we're going to win if we spend 14% less than they do.
transcript.zh: 我不知道这能否激励一线员工，但我确信这有助于一线员工明白公司的发展方向。我以前常开玩笑说，American Airlines 上一个座右铭其实非常难以向内部在职员工传达，但我打心底里觉得那是事实——那就是，“咱们的产品哪怕比 United 和 Delta 差上个 12%，但只要成本支出比他们少 14%，我们就赢了”。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Business-wise, that's an okay strategy, really hard to communicate. I think now, if people take Nat seriously, it means that no matter what you do at American, you know that in order to make money, you've got to spend money, and I do think it's important.
transcript.zh: 从商业逻辑上讲，这不失为一种策略，但极其难以下达贯彻。我认为现在，如果大家把 Nat 的话当回事，那就意味着无论你在 American 身处什么岗位，你都明白要想赚钱就必须先投入成本，我觉得这种认知非常关键。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: You know, when we were talking about this earlier, you mentioned there's the global aspect of this, there's also the premier aspect of this. So if we get beyond the "the" and maybe that is semantics, because this is saying, look, we are not going to be a ULCC, which was never going to happen anyway.
transcript.zh: 你知道，我们之前讨论这个的时候，你提到过这里面既有“全球化”的维度，也有“顶级”的维度。所以如果我们抛开那个冠词纠葛——或许那确实只是文字游戏——因为这番话的潜台词是：听着，我们绝不会变成一家超低成本航司（ULCC），虽然这本来也绝不可能发生。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: But it's also, as you were talking about, getting away from that idea before of we just have to cut costs. This is actually more of a revenue focus, which they have been talking about already, but they haven't coherently put that together, right?
transcript.zh: 但这也正如你所说，是在摆脱以往那种“我们只需一味削减成本”的思路。这实际上更侧重于创收端，虽然他们一直在提，但之前从未将这些碎片化想法系统连贯地串联起来，对吧？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: They've said, look, look at our new 787 with these great beds and Premium Economy and everything else. It's so nice. And look at our 777-300 that's now out with 70 flat beds, and everything is so great.
transcript.zh: 他们之前只是说，瞧瞧我们全新的 787，配有超棒的平躺睡床、超级经济舱等一应俱全，体验极佳。再看看我们改装后亮相的 777-300，配备了 70 张平躺床位，一切都非常棒。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: But it's always felt kind of piecemeal. So, now we've got this overarching strategy, which we can argue if it's good or bad.
transcript.zh: 但这感觉总有点零敲碎打。所以，现在我们有了这个宏观战略，虽然我们可以争论它到底是好是坏。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And then I think it gets into how do you start to execute this because you have the global piece and the premier piece. And so now you're trying to hit on multiple different things to try and ultimately still play catch-up, even if that's not what you want to do. That is kind of where we're going, right?
transcript.zh: 然后我认为问题就变成了你该如何着手执行，因为你既有全球网络的部分，又有高端定位的部分。所以现在你试图在多个不同方向上发力，最终仍是在苦苦追赶，即便这不是你的初衷。这大致就是未来的走向，对吧？

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: So, Brett, you actually spoke to Nat. I haven't spoken to Nat on the record in a long time. Did he tell you, with the two pieces of this, the premier part, which I see mostly as product, and then the global part, and American isn't really a global airline now, exactly how many billions of dollars they plan to spend over how much time in order to get where he's going?
transcript.zh: Brett，你最近确实和 Nat 聊过。我已经很久没有正式采访过 Nat 了。关于这两个板块——在我看来主要是硬件产品的高端部分，以及全球网络部分（毕竟美航现在算不上真正的全球航司）——他有没有告诉你，他们计划在多长时间内投入几十亿美元来达成他的目标？

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Because we're talking product improvements that just cost money. And oh, my gosh, the colossal money-losing routes this airline may have to start to truly be global.
transcript.zh: 因为我们所讨论的客舱产品升级纯粹就是烧钱。而且我的天，为了成为真正的全球航司，这家航司可能不得不开辟那些巨额亏损的航线。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Yeah, so we did not get into specific numbers. I think maybe that's a conversation I should have with Devon May, the CFO.
transcript.zh: 是的，我们没有谈到具体数字。我想这或许是我应该和首席财务官 Devon May 探讨的话题。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: I heard he's taken to his bed. He can't handle all the spending.
transcript.zh: 我听说他已经卧床不起了。他根本吃不消这么大的开销。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: I was going to say, I don't know.
transcript.zh: 我正想这么说呢，我也不好说。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: The poor guy, he gets out there in front of investors for how many years about cost control and everything, that man's head must be exploding.
transcript.zh: 这可怜的家伙，这么多年来一直在投资者面前大谈成本控制之类的话题，他的脑袋现在肯定要炸裂了。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: There's no question, because it's basically just like, "Approve everything." It doesn't matter what it is. I don't even know why they have a CFO now, frankly. I guess it's just required that you have one.
transcript.zh: 毫无疑问，因为现在基本上就是“通通批准”。不管是什么项目都批。坦白讲，我甚至不知道他们现在为什么还需要 CFO。大概只是规定必须设立这个职位吧。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: I will say this: there is a limit to what they will spend. I do know that, because I brought up the hypothetical of, "Hey, shouldn't you just go and buy a bunch of Embraer E2s and dominate that smaller gauge since the others aren't really focusing on that, and also Embraer will probably give you the deal of a century?"
transcript.zh: 不过有一点我要说明：他们的支出是有限度的。这一点我确实清楚，因为我曾提出过一个假设：“哎，难道你们不该直接去买一批巴航工业 E2，趁着别家都没怎么关注这个市场去称霸小座级机型吗？更何况巴航工业可能还会给你开出世纪大折扣。”

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And I asked him to tell me why that was wrong, and his response was, "Capital concerns." There is a limit to what they will spend. Now that is not part of the premier aspect, but there is a limit is all that I know.
transcript.zh: 我让他说说这想法错在哪，他的回答是“资本层面的顾虑”。他们的支出确实是有上限的。虽然这不属于高端定位的范畴，但我所知道的就是确实存在底线。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: But beyond that, right? I mean, they're doing the seatback screens, which is very expensive and time-consuming, to the point that we know Alaska said, "Nah, pass."
transcript.zh: 但除此之外呢？他们正在加装机上椅背个人屏幕，这项工程既耗资巨大又极其耗时，以至于我们知道阿拉斯加航空直接说了“算了吧，不搞”。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And then we have all the retrofits they're doing. There is a new widebody order coming. He told me it would be within the next two months. He would not even give me a hint as to whether it was Airbus versus Boeing, but these will all be very premium-heavy focused aircraft because that is what American is doing now.
transcript.zh: 然后他们还在推进所有的客舱翻新改装。接下来还会有一笔新的宽体机订单。他告诉我会在未来两个月内敲定。他甚至不愿透露到底是空客还是波音，但这些飞机都将极度偏向高端舱位配置，因为这正是美航目前的策略。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: So, that's however much money that's going to be just to acquire those widebodies alone. Like this is going to be a pretty enormous outlay just to get toward that premium piece.
transcript.zh: 所以，光是采购那些宽体机就得砸下大笔资金。单单为了实现向高端化迈进的这一步，这就将是一笔极其庞大的资本开支。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: If I have to say Scott Kirby's name again, I will. That man says there's only room for two premium airlines. And if we had him on the show today, he might say something about, "Okay, they can spend their billions and billions of dollars to match
transcript.zh: 如果非要我再提一次 Scott Kirby 的名字，那我就提吧。那个人曾说市场上只容得下两家高端全服务航司。如果今天请他上节目，他可能会说：“行啊，他们大可以砸下几十上百亿美元去跟进

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Just, but there's only room for two, and American is wasting its money. Did you get into that at all with that?
transcript.zh: 但市场上只容得下两家，American 这是在白白浪费钱。关于这点你跟他深聊了吗？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Actually, there was a moment where I brought that up and I said, 'Listen, Nat, so, you know, Scott Kirby says there's only room for two.' And his response is, 'Yeah, but he didn't say which two.'
transcript.zh: 事实上我还真提到了这点。我说：'Nat 你听着，Scott Kirby 可说过市场只容得下两家。' 他的回答是：'对啊，但他可没说是哪两家。'

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Which that was a joke, but he's certainly aware of this, that Scott's assertion that there is only room for two. I think that is probably not true, personally.
transcript.zh: 这虽然是个玩笑话，但他显然很清楚 Scott 所谓'只容得下两家'的断言。我个人认为这大概并不符合事实。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Now, when you get into the question, this again about bringing global into it, then this is where maybe that is the case, right? But, you know, is there room for Alaska to be a premium airline? I think there is.
transcript.zh: 不过一旦切入这个问题，也就是把全球化网络纳入考量时，事情可能确实如此。但如果问市场上是否有空间容纳 Alaska 成为一家高端航司？我认为是有的。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: They're not a true global carrier. That doesn't mean there's not room for a premium carrier, and this is where I'm really curious about. Because I think we all know with Scott, his whole goal is to get that message out there.
transcript.zh: 他们算不上真正的全球型航司，但这并不意味着高端航司没有生存空间，这也正是我非常好奇的地方。因为大家都清楚 Scott 的风格，他的核心目标就是要把这种论调宣扬出去。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Which works great for him, because other CEOs are quiet and don't say anything. So, Scott can say these things and will it to be true in the minds of investors, in the minds of Wall Street, wherever it may be. That's his goal.
transcript.zh: 这招对他屡试不爽，因为其他航司的 CEO 都三缄其口、不发一言。所以 Scott 可以在外大放厥词，并在投资者、华尔街的心目中把这塑造成既定事实。这就是他的算盘。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: It doesn't mean it is true, but it means it's what he wants to be true. And I think we probably know why he's saying that.
transcript.zh: 这并不代表它就是事实，只是他希望这成为事实而已。我想大家也都很清楚他为什么要这么说。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Absolutely. And when he started saying this, whatever it was a couple of years ago, this question hadn't really come to the forefront yet. It was more of an academic question, there were only two airlines trying to do this, and that was United and Delta.
transcript.zh: 确实如此。大约两年前他刚开始这么说的时候，这个问题还没有真正引起大家的关注。当时这更像是一个纯理论探讨，因为那时尝试走这条路子的只有两家航司——United 和 Delta。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: At this point, we're going to see if Scott's math is right, because as you said, Alaska is going premium and global, though in a smaller way, and American seems to be headed there. So, can all four last?
transcript.zh: 事到如今，我们倒要看看 Scott 的小算盘到底对不对了。因为正如你所说，Alaska 正在往高端和全球化方向发力（尽管体量较小），而 American 似乎也正朝着这个方向靠拢。那么，四家航司都能撑下去吗？

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Like you, I don't see why not, assuming that this market has changed in the way that Shane Tackett told us it has, both privately and on the podcast a few weeks ago. The Alaska folks essentially said that their customers want premium, they're willing to pay for it.
transcript.zh: 我和你的看法一样，看不出有什么不可以，前提是市场确实发生了 Shane Tackett 前几周私下以及在播客里告诉我们的那种转变。Alaska 的管理层明确表示，他们的旅客需要高端服务，并且愿意为此买单。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: And these airlines like American and Alaska, they're no longer taking a chance on going upmarket. They're literally doing exactly what their customers tell them that they want.
transcript.zh: 像 American 和 Alaska 这样的航司，进军高端市场已不再是在赌博，而完全是旅客要什么他们就提供什么。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: I think there is something of a risk here in that there is a long lead time to do a lot of this work. We can look at American installing in-seat video, which isn't even going to start for a couple years, won't be done until the next decade.
transcript.zh: 我认为这里面其实潜藏着一定风险，因为很多改造项目的交付周期实在太长了。比如看 American 计划加装机上座椅个人屏幕，不仅要过几年才启动，甚至要拖到下个年代才能全部完工。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: We can look at the widebody order, which, unless there's some miracle, none of those planes are going to come in until the next decade, just because of the backlog that's going on. So you are making decisions now on some of these things that will hit you several years down the line when we have no idea what the world's going to look like.
transcript.zh: 再看看宽体机订单，除非出现奇迹，否则由于目前严重的储备订单积压，那些飞机在未来十年内根本无法交付。因此，你现在敲定的某些决策，要等好几年后才会真正落地生效，而到那时世界格局会变成什么样谁也说不准。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: On the other hand, it does seem pretty clear that this is a long-standing trend. When did Delta start doing this?
transcript.zh: 但换个角度看，这显然已经是一个长期确立的行业趋势了。Delta 是从什么时候开始这么干的？

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: 20 years ago? Yeah. Look, the Alaska folks are a little bit more publicly honest than the American folks.
transcript.zh: 二十年前？是的。你看，Alaska 的人往往比 American 的人更愿意对外吐露实情。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: You talk about long lead time, and that was the argument from a couple of these airlines in 2016, 2017, 2018. "Well, if we do it now, the trend might end, and we won't have these airplanes outfitted until 2027."
transcript.zh: 你刚才提到交付周期很长，而这正是几家航司在 2016、2017、2018 年的说辞：“如果我们现在改舱，这一潮流可能很快就结束了，而且我们改装完这些飞机都得等到 2027 年了。”

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Well, now it's almost 2027 and you wish you could have acted then. They've seen this trend go on for 9-10 years past then, and now it's like, "Okay, well maybe in 2035 this will end, but we've been wrong every year over the last 10 years, and we got to try it now." It's too late to pretend that things are going to go back to, quote, "normal" at some point.
transcript.zh: 可现在眼看就要到 2027 年了，你反而后悔当年没下手。他们眼睁睁看着这股趋势又持续了九到十年，现在又变成了：“行吧，也许到 2035 年这股风就过去了，但过去十年里我们年年都预判失误，现在必须硬着头皮上了。”如今再幻想行情有朝一日能重回所谓的“常态”，未免为时已晚。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: I think you're right. I do think with Alaska, though, you know, not putting in-seat video in on, like, the MAX 10, there is something to be said for that. We can argue it either way.
transcript.zh: 我觉得你说得对。不过就 Alaska 而言，比如他们不在 MAX 10 上装机载座椅屏幕这件事，其实还是有值得探讨的道理的。无论正方反方，大家都能辩出几分理来。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: But for them to say, look, it's a really long lead time. We don't know what screen technology is going to be like then. We might just end up putting something on there that's out of date and it's going to delay us getting this airplane into service.
transcript.zh: 但他们表示，现在的交货周期实在太长，根本吃不准未来的屏幕技术会发展成什么样。万一最后装上去的是一套过时的设备，反而还会拖累这款飞机投入商业运营的时间。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: You know, maybe that is more of a of an acknowledgement of the potential risk that's out there. It's not the part about going premium. I don't think that is a risk.
transcript.zh: 或许这更多是对潜在风险的一种正视。问题并不在于追求两舱高端化，我觉得高端化本身并不算什么风险。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And that's why I think if you're American, what are your other choices? Because the last effort to go cost focused clearly did not work to generate the returns that other airlines are getting.
transcript.zh: 正因如此，换作你是 American，你还能有别的出路吗？毕竟上一轮把重心全压在压降成本上的尝试，显然没能带来其他航司那样的收益表现。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: No, I don't think there is another option. It's great to have somebody like Nat come in from the outside—and we presume this is the case, because there was inertia before he got there and now there isn't—push the company to move with the times and add some touches that help it match Delta and United, and, you know, make it a premier global airline. Maybe not *the*, but certainly *a*.
transcript.zh: 确实没有其他退路了。像 Nat 这样从外部空降一位能人挺好的——我们推测也是如此，因为在他来之前公司暮气沉沉、存在路径依赖，而现在这种惰性不复存在了——他推动公司与时俱进，打磨细节以向 Delta 和 United 看齐，并将它打造成一家顶尖的全球性航司。也许做不到行业第一，但至少能位列头部梯队。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: There is one other strategy that I think might work pretty well, possibly even better.
transcript.zh: 我倒觉得还有另一条路径可能会走得通，甚至成效更显著。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: I have no idea if there's a joke coming here or you're serious.
transcript.zh: 我真吃不准你这是要抖包袱，还是在说正经的。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: It's not really a joke. I think the strategy that they could follow if they wanted to is sell to United. And it's like I say, it's not really a joke in that I am sure United would love to hear that. I don't know if it could ever be pushed through.
transcript.zh: 倒也不完全是玩笑话。我认为如果他们真愿意的话，可以走的一条路线就是：把自己打包卖给 United。正如我刚才所言，这并非纯粹开玩笑，United 听到肯定求之不得。虽然我不知道这在反垄断层面能否获批。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: But American has spent so much time denying the trends that are out there that it's got so much work to do and so much money to be invested. This is where I think it starts to get to be a little a little dicier on what is the right way forward, but maybe that's just silly.
transcript.zh: 但 American 之前花了太长时间去否定市场大势，以至于现在积重难返，需要补的功课和砸的资金实在太多了。正是在这一点上，关于未来到底该走哪条路，局面才开始变得愈发棘手，不过或许我这也纯粹是异想天开了。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: You didn't have the chutzpah to ask Nat on the record about the proposed United acquisition, did you?
transcript.zh: 你当时没胆量在正式采访录音里直接去问 Nat，关于被 United 收购的构想吧？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: I did not, but I'm pretty sure that one is going to be above his pay grade, so did not worry about that one. All right, Brian, so we've talked about the premier...
transcript.zh: 我确实没问。不过我敢肯定这种事远超他的职权范围，所以干脆就没去操那份闲心。好了，Brian，既然我们聊完了这些顶尖……

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: clear premium piece. But we haven't really talked about the global as much. So, let's take a break, and then I want to talk about that and what that means for the network.
transcript.zh: 清晰的高端定位。但我们其实还没怎么聊过全球航线网络这部分。所以，我们先进一段广告，稍后我想聊聊这方面，以及这对航线网络意味着什么。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: So Brett, I know you aren't our resident mileage buyer, but have you bought any this quarter?
transcript.zh: Brett，我知道你平时不怎么买里程积分，不过这个季度你有买过吗？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Your timing is great. I was just looking at joining my wife on a business trip. Fares are high, and my mileage options are slim.
transcript.zh: 你问得太巧了。我正打算陪我太太去出差。机票价格很高，而且我能用的里程兑换选项也很有限。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: The only thing I found was on an airline that doesn't transfer from any of my credit card point programs. So I was actually looking at buying miles to boost my balance.
transcript.zh: 我唯一找到的余票属于一家无法从我任何信用卡积分转点的航司。所以我确实正在考虑直接购买里程来补足账户余额。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: You're not alone. A lot of members are doing exactly that, especially when there's a trip they really want to take.
transcript.zh: 你不是一个人。很多会员都在这么做，尤其是在遇到特别想去的一趟旅行时。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Buying miles helps get there faster. And in cases like mine, it's the difference between being able to take a trip or not going at all.
transcript.zh: 购买里程能让你更快达成目标。而在我这种情况下，它直接决定了我能成行还是根本去不了。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And if I think I have enough, but reach checkout a few miles short, there's also the top-up option, which closes the gap right there.
transcript.zh: 如果我觉得自己积分差不多够了，但结账时却发现还差那么几英里，还可以选择补足充值选项，当场就能填补差额。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: And buyers like you aren't just generating incremental revenue. They tend to redeem more, fly more, and stay active longer.
transcript.zh: 像你这样的买家不仅能为航司带来增量收入。他们往往还会兑换更多里程、飞行更频繁，并且保持会员活跃度的时间也更长。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: That's what Buy and Top-Up from Points, a Plusgrade company, are built for. And because Points works across more than 60 loyalty programs and a billion-plus members, every partner benefits from what they learn about what actually converts.
transcript.zh: 这正是 Plusgrade 旗下 Points 平台的购买与充值功能所擅长的。由于 Points 服务于 60 多个常旅客计划和超过 10 亿会员，每家合作伙伴都能从中获益，了解究竟什么才能真正促成转化。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Because the moment a member like you decides that they want to go is exactly when a program should be ready to meet them.
transcript.zh: 因为当像你这样的会员动身启程的那一刻，常旅客计划就必须做好随时响应的准备。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Buy and Top-Up from Points, a Plusgrade company, help members close the gap between the balance they have and the reward they want. Learn more at plusgrade.com.
transcript.zh: Plusgrade 旗下 Points 的购买与充值方案，帮助会员填补现有余额与心仪奖励之间的差距。欢迎访问 plusgrade.com 了解详情。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: You know I love digging into data, so I am thrilled to have SkyGo as a sponsor. But today, I want to focus on pretty pictures instead of data.
transcript.zh: 你知道我一向喜欢深挖数据，所以非常高兴能有 SkyGo 作为赞助商。不过今天，我想把焦点从数据转到那些精美的图表上。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Sorry, what?
transcript.zh: 等等，什么图？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Okay, not pictures, maps. SkyMaps, actually. For example, we've spent a lot of time recently talking about Alaska, Hawaiian, and where that network story goes next.
transcript.zh: 好吧，不是普通的图片，是航线地图，确切地说是 SkyMaps。例如，我们最近花了很多时间讨论阿拉斯加航空、夏威夷航空，以及他们航线网络接下来的走向。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: What I like about SkyGo's SkyMap feature is that you can actually see that story unfold, not just talk about it.
transcript.zh: 我喜欢 SkyGo 的 SkyMap 功能的一点在于，你能亲眼看到整个网络格局的演变过程，而不仅仅是纸上谈兵。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Ah, I see what you're talking about. And yes, it's great to be able to pull up an older Alaska Airlines network and put it next to Alaska today, and then add Hawaiian, or take it a step further and bring in Aloha's historical network too.
transcript.zh: 啊，我懂你的意思了。确实，能调出阿拉斯加航空以前的网络，并与现在的阿拉斯加航空并列对比，然后再叠加上夏威夷航空，甚至更进一步调出阿罗哈航空（Aloha）的历史航线网络，这体验太棒了。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Right. It's easy to just keep going down that rabbit hole because now you're not just thinking about one route. You're looking at how these different networks fit together, where they overlap, and what's changed across time.
transcript.zh: 没错。你很容易就会沉浸其中越挖越深，因为此时你思考的不再只是单条航线。你在观察这些不同网络是如何契合拼接的、它们在哪里重叠，以及随时间推移发生了哪些变化。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And you can compare four airline or airport networks at once, either layered or in split views.
transcript.zh: 而且你可以同时对比四家航司或机场的航线网络，既能图层叠加对比，也能分屏查看。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: If only you could then design your own, nerd.
transcript.zh: 要是还能自己在上面画航线规划就好了，你这个航线宅。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: You can! You can actually add hypothetical routes right on the map, right next to the existing networks if you want.
transcript.zh: 还真能！你完全可以直接在地图上添加设想中的航线，想加在现有网络旁边都可以。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Then add a range overlay from any airport and see which places fall within a distance you choose.
transcript.zh: 然后从任意机场添加航程覆盖圈，看看在你设定的航距范围内都涵盖了哪些目的地。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: So you can go from "where did they fly?" to "what about a route over here?" without leaving the map?
transcript.zh: 所以你完全不需要跳出地图界面，就能从研究“他们以前飞过哪”，直接切换到规划“要是在这开条航线会怎样”？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Yep. If you've been following the Alaska and Hawaiian discussion on this show, SkyMap is a great way to go explore that story for yourself.
transcript.zh: 没错。如果你一直在听我们节目中关于阿拉斯加与夏威夷航空合并的讨论，SkyMap 是你自己亲自深入探索这一网络演变的绝佳工具。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: The networks you remember, the routes you imagine, explore SkyMap in SkyGo. Visit theairshowpodcast.com/skygo for more information.
transcript.zh: 重温你记忆中的航网，规划你设想中的航线，尽在 SkyGo 的 SkyMap。欢迎访问 theairshowpodcast.com/skygo 了解更多信息。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: And we're back. Brett, in the first part of this episode, we talked about the premium part of Pieper's comments. To get American to be a truly premium airline, billions of dollars will have to be spent.
transcript.zh: 我们回来了。Brett，在本集的前半部分，我们探讨了 Pieper 关于高端化定位的言论。要让美航成为一家真正的高端全服务航司，必须投入数十亿美元。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: But there's a roadmap to how you do that. Other airlines have done it. We know what American needs.
transcript.zh: 但这方面是有现成路线图可循的。其他航司已经做到过，我们也清楚美航需要补足什么。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: The second part of Pieper's comments are actually a little harder to get, cuz he says that he wants American to be a global airline, right? The global airline.
transcript.zh: 但 Pieper 言论的第二部分实际上更令人费解，因为他说希望美航成为一家全球性航司，对吧？成为“那家”真正的全球性航司。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Sadly, at some point American became an airline that flies to Latin America and Europe and like Tokyo. So how are we going to fill in those gaps?
transcript.zh: 令人唏嘘的是，美航在某个节点上沦为了一家只飞拉丁美洲、欧洲，外加类似东京等少数航点的航司。那么，我们该如何填补这些网络空白呢？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: If you want to fulfill the vision, you have to be number one in at least one of the big US markets. Because that's how you get the credit card spend, that's how all the things start moving, right?
transcript.zh: 如果你想实现这一愿景，就必须在至少一个美国核心大型枢纽市场做到第一。因为只有这样才能带动联名信用卡消费，所有业务飞轮才能真正转动起来，对吧？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And so I talked to Nat about this, saying, "How are you going to do this?" And the winner is LAX, Brian. We are going to benefit from this. LAX will be bulked up.
transcript.zh: 所以我跟 Nat 聊到了这一点，问他：“你们打算怎么做？”最终选定的核心就是洛杉矶国际机场（LAX），Brian。我们会从中受益，LAX 航线网络将得到大幅扩充。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Okay. So, do I have this right, Brett? Cuz you said that you have to be number one in some major market, and American is number one in Miami, which is a major market. It has a lot of routes. It flies into Latin America. It used to have more.
transcript.zh: 好吧。那 Brett，我理解的对吗？你说必须在某个核心枢纽市场做到第一，而美航在迈阿密就是第一，这本身就是个核心市场。它拥有大量航线，深耕拉丁美洲，以前航点还要更多。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: It has at times been a money-producing machine. And you're telling me that we're going to ignore that hub and focus mostly on what, a transpacific operation from Los Angeles, where American over the years has lost a colossal amount of money, and where it would in the future perhaps lose even more money? Do I have that right?
transcript.zh: 那里一度是一台印钞机。而你现在告诉我，我们要忽视那个枢纽，转而主要聚焦于从洛杉矶出发的跨太平洋航线？美航多年来在洛杉矶亏得一塌糊涂，未来甚至可能亏损得更惨？我理解得没错吧？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Not quite, but almost. No, okay, I was talking about the big three US markets, the New York, Chicago, LA. But Miami, yes, very important, and he did talk about how American, during its Sun Market focus post-pandemic, that happened at the expense of other hubs.
transcript.zh: 不完全是，但也差不多了。好吧，我刚才指的是美国前三大核心航空市场：纽约、芝加哥和洛杉矶。但迈阿密确实非常重要，他也确实谈到了美航在疫情后聚焦“阳光带”休闲市场时，是如何以牺牲其他枢纽为代价的。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And they did suffer with local traffic in places like Philly and Miami, and of course we know Chicago. So he did say that Miami will be a focus.
transcript.zh: 他们在费城、迈阿密，当然还有我们熟知的芝加哥等地的本地客源市场都遭受了损失。所以他明确表示迈阿密依然会是一个重心。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: You know, I pushed more on that, why were the XLRs not put into Latin first? I wrote this up. This is where I think you zag when the others zig, and can find a better place for yourself, you play to your strengths.
transcript.zh: 我也就此进一步追问：为什么不先把 A321XLR 投放到拉美航线？我还就此写过文章。我认为在这种情况下，别人往东你就该往西，发挥自身长处，为自己找到更有利的生态位。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: I didn't really get an answer to that question, it's just Europe came first, basically. But this is not at the expense of Miami and Latin.
transcript.zh: 对此我并没有得到确切的答复，基本上就是欧洲航线被排在了最优先的位置。但这并不是以牺牲迈阿密和拉美市场为代价的。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: However, this is going to suck up a lot of resources. Unquestionably, it's going to lose a lot of money.
transcript.zh: 然而，这势必会消耗大量的资源。毫无疑问，这在初期肯定会亏损大笔资金。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: during the build-out process and I don't know how long that will be. But clearly, Nat feels it is time for American to take another run at the crown by reopening this LAX Pacific gateway that it closed during the pandemic.
transcript.zh: 在改扩建工程期间——我不知道这还得持续多久。但显然，Nat 认为现在是时候让美航重振旗鼓了，他们想重新开放疫情期间关闭的洛杉矶（LAX）太平洋门户。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Brett, let me say this as clearly as I can. I think that we run the greatest airline podcast in the history of the world. The.
transcript.zh: Brett，我尽量把话说明白点。我认为我们做出了全世界有史以来最牛的航空播客。绝无仅有。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: And I think with our, with our multi-part series on what is wrong with American Airlines, we, by ourselves, pushed the airline to make changes to its marketing and brand and premium strategy.
transcript.zh: 而且我觉得，正是凭借我们针对美国航空问题所在所做的那几期连载节目，单靠我们自己，就倒逼这家航司调整了其市场营销、品牌和高端客舱策略。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: So I know people in Dallas-Fort Worth are listening to this show. So let me tell them very directly: Do not do this. Hasn't American had enough by now in Los Angeles?
transcript.zh: 所以我知道达拉斯-沃斯堡总部的人都在听这档播客。那我就把话挑明了跟他们说：千万别这么干。美航在洛杉矶吃的苦头难道还不够多吗？

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Brett, we live in Southern California. American tried this at LAX in the 2010s, very, very, very bad.
transcript.zh: Brett，我们都住在南加州。美航在 2010 年代就曾在 LAX 试过这么干，结果可以说是非常、非常、非常惨烈。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Now technically, this flying stopped quote 'in the pandemic'. But that was a nice little excuse because these routes, many of them, Shanghai, Hong Kong, where else were they flying?
transcript.zh: 从表面上看，这些航班是所谓“因疫情”停飞的。但这不过是个体面的借口罢了，因为那些航线——比如上海、香港，他们当时还飞哪儿来着？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Beijing, I think, was the worst.
transcript.zh: 北京航线，我觉得那条最惨。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: These routes were not very good. And I remember asking somebody in American right about April 2020, when airlines were saying, 'Oh, we're suspending these flights, and they're coming back.'
transcript.zh: 这些航线的表现根本不行。我记得在 2020 年 4 月左右问过美航内部的人，当时各大航司都声称：‘噢，我们只是暂停这些航班，以后还会恢复的。’

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: And this insider said to me, 'Brian, they're never coming back, because if you knew how much money they were losing, you would know this is a nice, clever excuse.'
transcript.zh: 但这位内部人士对我说：‘Brian，它们永远不可能恢复了。如果你知道他们亏了多少钱，就会明白这只是个顺水推舟的聪明借口。’

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: So I don't see why these routes are going to perform any better now from LAX. In fact, I would imagine they'd perform worse because Delta and United are dueling it out for transpacific supremacy from here.
transcript.zh: 所以我不明白这些航线现在从 LAX 出发凭什么能有更好的表现。实际上，我觉得只会更差，因为达美和美联航正在这里争夺跨太平洋航线的霸主地位。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Brett, please tell me that Nat didn't give you that old talking point about how no airline can actually win in LAX?
transcript.zh: Brett，快告诉我 Nat 没拿那套‘没有任何航司能在 LAX 真正称霸’的老生常谈来敷衍你吧？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: I'm going to need to step back for a second and address a couple things in here from that soliloquy, shall we call it. First of all, I think that is exactly why people listen to this podcast. It's the humility.
transcript.zh: 我得先打断一下，回应你刚才那段独白里的几点。首先，我认为大家听我们这档播客正是看中了这一点——那就是我们的谦虚。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: I think we've really got that nailed. And, you know, everyone, you're welcome for the gift that we are to you.
transcript.zh: 我觉得咱们把谦逊这块拿捏得死死的。各位听众，不用客气，能听到我们的播客就是送给你们的恩赐。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: What was it that that former Canadian airline CEO said about our work? It wasn't, it wasn't very kind.
transcript.zh: 之前那位前加拿大某航司 CEO 是怎么评价我们的？他的话可一点都不客气。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: At WestJet.
transcript.zh: 西捷航空（WestJet）那位。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Something about how he was the former CEO and we were armchair quarterbacks and we do not deserve to ask these questions?
transcript.zh: 好像是说他才是正牌前 CEO，而我们不过是纸上谈兵的键盘侠，根本没资格提这些问题？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: That's right. It was the 'man in the arena' quote from Teddy Roosevelt. Anyway, back to the point here. Yes, of course Nat said that, but honestly, he's right. Nobody can win LA.
transcript.zh: 没错，他搬出了西奥多·罗斯福那段‘角斗场中的勇士’名言。不管怎样，言归正传。没错，Nat 确实那么说了，但平心而论，他说得对。没有任何航司能在洛杉矶称霸。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: It's just not an option, just because of the way that this has been constructed over time. But that's sort of a double-edged sword. In one sense, it means that no
transcript.zh: 这根本不可能办到，完全是由于这里长久以来的竞争格局所决定的。但这其实是一把双刃剑。一方面，这意味着没有任何——

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: American cannot win, but somebody has to be number one, and it means nobody is ever ahead of you too far in theory, so you still have that chance to regain the crown, which, by the way, American had until the pandemic.
transcript.zh: 美航不可能赢，但总得有人排第一。这意味着在理论上，没有人能真正把你甩开太远，你始终有机会夺回王座——顺便说一句，美航在疫情爆发前一直稳坐这个位置。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Which crown are we talking about? Departures, ASMs, are we talking about the crown in overall money lost in Los Angeles? Because those are three separate things. You can be number one in a lot of things and still lose your shirt.
transcript.zh: 我们说的是哪个王座？是起飞架次、可用座英里（ASM），还是在洛杉矶整体亏损额的头把交椅？因为这是截然不同的三码事。你可以在很多指标上争第一，但依旧赔得底裤都不剩。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: I think American had all three. But this is what this comes down to, though: if you want to be the global whatever we're calling it, you have to have a Pacific operation.
transcript.zh: 我觉得美航这三项都占全了。不过说到底，事情的关键在于：如果你想成为所谓的“真正全球性航司”，你就必须拥有跨太平洋航线网络。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: I thought that was based in Dallas-Fort Worth. Did that not work?
transcript.zh: 我以为美航的亚太枢纽设在达拉斯-沃斯堡。难道这条路走不通吗？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: There's very little out of Dallas-Fort Worth, there's almost nothing there. You know, they serve the big cities and partner hubs and stuff, but that's kind of it, and I don't think there's much opportunity to go beyond that.
transcript.zh: 达拉斯-沃斯堡出发的跨太航线极少，几乎可以说微乎其微。他们只飞几个核心大城市和合作伙伴的枢纽，也就仅此而已了，我认为很难再有进一步拓展的空间。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: So, what do you do? You need to find a place to put it, and your least bad option is LA. And then it also comes together with this point of, well, we need to be big in LA, since we can't really get New York or Chicago.
transcript.zh: 那该怎么办呢？你得找个地方来布局，而洛杉矶就是你“最不差”的选择。紧接着逻辑又回到了原点：既然我们在纽约和芝加哥都占不到便宜，那我们在洛杉矶就必须做大。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: So, this is our our last stand, and we're going to leave it all out there, and lose a bunch of money if we have to, to get to this end game. But if that is your vision, then I don't really know how else you go about doing it.
transcript.zh: 所以这是我们的背水一战，哪怕孤注一掷、蒙受巨额亏损，也要杀到终局。但如果这就是你的宏图愿景，我真不知道除了硬着头皮上还能怎么做。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And we can argue the vision is maybe corrupted from what it should be if they stick too close to that, and goes back from "the" premium global to "a" premium global, or not even global.
transcript.zh: 我们当然可以争论，如果他们一条道走到黑，其战略定位或许就偏离了正轨，从“唯一首选的高端全球航司”沦为“平庸的全球航司之一”，甚至根本称不上全球性航司。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: I'm just wondering, Brett, have you have you cherry-picked any data that shows this might be a decent idea instead of a terrible one? What do you got for our listeners?
transcript.zh: 我只是很好奇，Brett，你有没有专门挑选过某些数据，能证明这或许是个不错的点子，而不是一出彻头彻尾的灾难？你为听众准备了哪些干货？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Well, there's a lot of data out there, and you know that's what I live for. LAX is, I would say unquestionably, the most competitive airport, big airport, in the US, if not the world.
transcript.zh: 市面上数据多得很，你知道我向来就是靠挖掘数据为生的。我认为毫无疑问，洛杉矶国际机场（LAX）全美、乃至全球竞争最激烈的大型机场。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And if we look at it today, or actually if we go back and look at for all of 2025 in the domestic market from the DOT's O&D data—so we're looking at local passengers, not connecting.
transcript.zh: 如果我们审视当下，或者确切地说，回顾美国交通部（DOT）2025年国内始发与终到（O&D）全年的数据——我们这里看的是本地始发旅客，不包含中转客流。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Delta was number one; it carried 23.7% of the local market. American and United were just under 20%, Southwest near 15%, Alaska was just under 10%.
transcript.zh: 达美航空位居榜首，占据了本地市场23.7%的份额。美航和美联航均略低于20%，美西南接近15%，阿拉斯加航空则略低于10%。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: That is a lot of airlines trying to be close to the top, and it does show that you can't really get there. Interestingly, if you look at some of the other airports that are around, they're not in this area.
transcript.zh: 有这么多家航司都在拼命争抢头部交椅，这也证明谁都不可能真正独霸一方。有趣的是，如果你观察周边其他机场，情况完全不同。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: The closest in the US, that would be in Florida, some of those airports. But those are different because those are mostly people coming to those airports from elsewhere, and it's really that variety that matters to the origin traffic.
transcript.zh: 全美情况最接近的反倒在佛罗里达州的某些机场。但两者的性质截然不同，因为佛罗里达的机场主要接待外地涌入的进港旅客，而对于始发客流来说，航线与航司的多样性才至关重要。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: The destination traffic, you may have a lot of different airlines coming from a lot of different places, but it doesn't mean...
transcript.zh: 在目的地市场，你可能会看到形形色色的航司从天南海北飞过来，但这并不意味着……

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And that there's enough optionality for the local passenger. So the point is it is a wide open market in that sense. But it is a wide open market that you have multiple airlines gunning for the same thing.
transcript.zh: 而且对于当地旅客来说有足够多的选择。所以关键在于，从这个角度看它是一个完全开放的市场。但这也是一个多家航空公司都在争夺同一块蛋糕的完全开放市场。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: What about globally? You're pretty much talking about domestic.
transcript.zh: 那国际航线呢？你刚才基本都在说国内市场。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Globally, it's not much different.
transcript.zh: 国际航线上其实也没多大差别。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: All right, let's agree that LAX is very competitive, and no airline has ever been able to move ahead for a long time. I think that's probably by design and something that's important to the airport. They love their competition, they love their cheap fares. And this goes back throughout history, right?
transcript.zh: 好吧，我们都认同 LAX 竞争极度激烈，而且从来没有哪家航司能长期独占鳌头。我觉得这大概也是机场有意为之，对其非常重要。他们喜欢竞争，喜欢低廉的票价。这种局面也是由来已久了，对吧？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Yeah, it does. Of course, I went into the SkyHero schedule data here. And if we go back to the early '80s, the big airlines in LAX were United, Western, and PSA. So that's how it started.
transcript.zh: 是的，确实如此。我当然去查了查这里的 SkyHero 航班时刻数据。如果我们回到 80 年代初，当时 LAX 的主要航司是美联航、西方航空和太平洋西南航空。最初就是这样的格局。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: But then once the '80s got going, that's when the fight really picked up. So you had mergers, asset sales, regionals, all of this stuff. So by 1990, now you had kind of a Big Four. You had American, Delta, United, and USAir. But even combined, they still had fewer than 70% of departures back then.
transcript.zh: 但随着 80 年代的推进，战火真正被点燃了。于是出现了并购、资产出售、支线航司等各种变动。所以到了 1990 年，基本上形成了“四大航”格局：美航、达美、美联航和全美航空。但即便是它们加在一起，当年的离港航班量占比也依然不足 70%。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: USAir dropped out pretty quickly. In the '90s, Delta kind of pulled back, and then it really became American, United, and Southwest were the big guys at LAX.
transcript.zh: 全美航空很快就退出了。到了 90 年代，达美也有所收缩，之后 LAX 的主导者真正变成了美航、美联航和西南航空。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: So then as you get further on, there's still consolidation in the domestic markets, as there are everywhere. In the international market, especially in the Pacific, you don't have that same kind of consolidation that you have over in Europe, which we talked about this last week, right?
transcript.zh: 随着时间推移，国内市场同其他地方一样持续整合。但在国际市场，特别是在太平洋航线上，并没有出现像欧洲那样程度的整合，我们上周也讨论过这个，对吧？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: So you have every Chinese airline in the world flying to LAX. You have multiple airlines in Japan, in Korea. You have, I think, only three airlines in Taiwan—only three! But you have all these airlines that are flying to LAX because that's where the people from Asia want to go in the US.
transcript.zh: 所以你能看到几乎所有中国航司都飞 LAX。日本、韩国也有好几家航司在飞。台湾好像“只有”三家航司——居然只有三家！但所有这些航司都飞 LAX，因为那是亚洲旅客入境美国的首选目的地。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And so fares are low, you have just a ton of competition. And with that backdrop, the US carriers had tended to look elsewhere. They looked further from LAX. You had United building up San Francisco, Delta went into Seattle, and American didn't really know what to do, so it tried LAX. And that you've already talked about how great of an idea you think that was at the time.
transcript.zh: 因此票价低廉，竞争极为惨烈。在这种背景下，美国本土航司往往倾向于另寻出路，把目光投向 LAX 以外的地方。美联航发力旧金山枢纽，达美进军西雅图，而美航当时不知道该怎么办，于是尝试了 LAX。你之前已经说过，你觉得他们当时的这个决定有多“明智”了。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Well Brett, it's great that you've given us the history, it's great that you've given some data. And maybe if you only look at that stuff, you think to yourself, 'Oh, there's a opportunity in LAX. Nobody owns the market, nobody has that many more gates than another airline. It's perhaps on paper the best possible transpacific gateway for American.'
transcript.zh: 好吧 Brett，你为我们梳理了历史背景和数据，这很好。如果单看这些表面数据，你可能会想：‘哦，LAX 充满机遇，没人垄断这个市场，谁手里的登机口也没比别人多多少。从纸面上看，这可能是美航最好的跨太平洋门户。’

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: But even though you're smarter than I am, Brett, I think you have one problem, and that's you always underestimate the internal machinations of the airline industry, which I might call the 'aggressive man theory', okay? If you're United and Delta, you're making
transcript.zh: 但 Brett，虽然你比我聪明，我认为你忽视了一个问题，那就是你总是低估了航空业内部的权力运作与博弈，我称之为‘好胜心法则’，懂吗？如果你是美联航和达美，你手握充裕

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: pretty good profits system-wide, at least compared to other airlines. And you can run what, I think what do we call them, spite flights? Is that what we came up with?
transcript.zh: 全网络利润相当可观，至少和其他航司比是这样。而且你还可以开航线，我们管它叫什么来着，“报复性航班”？我们之前是这么说的吧？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Sure.
transcript.zh: 没错。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Like, you don't have to win LAX. It's nice to win LAX. You just have to ruin American.
transcript.zh: 比如，你不一定非得拿下洛杉矶机场（LAX）。能拿下 LAX 固然好，但只要能搞砸美国航空就行。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: So, American comes up with some sort of route at LAX, you just fly on top of them, you just mess with them on pricing strategy. Like, that is a big part of this.
transcript.zh: 如果美航在 LAX 开了一条航线，你就直接重叠排班飞压制他们，在定价策略上恶心他们。这在很大程度上就是竞争手段。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: And let me tell you that if Patrick Quayle and Joe Esposito decide that they don't want a third transpacific competitor at LAX, those guys are going to make their displeasure known, and it's going to be, what's your favorite word, a bloodbath.
transcript.zh: 而且我敢说，要是 Patrick Quayle 和 Joe Esposito 认定 LAX 不需要第三家跨太平洋竞争者，他们一定会把这种不满明确表现出来，那到时候就会演变成你最常说的那个词——血流成河。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Mmm, I do love a good bloodbath.
transcript.zh: 嗯，我确实喜欢看血流成河的戏码。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Just wait until that skirmish in Hong Kong.
transcript.zh: 等到香港那场交锋时就知道了。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Oh no, that's the way you lose so much money. I mean, Delta is probably finding that out right now too, but the thing is, is that it's not as straightforward.
transcript.zh: 哎呀，那种打法亏钱亏得太狠了。我觉得达美航空现在大概也体会到了，但问题在于，事情并没那么简单直接。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And first of all, I don't underestimate [laughter] United and Delta here. I have no doubt that they are probably smiling and are joyfully plotting where they're going to put airplanes. But there is more to that here.
transcript.zh: 首先，我绝不低估美联航和达美。我毫不怀疑他们此刻可能正一边冷笑，一边得意地盘算着把飞机往哪儿调。但这里面还有更多门道。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: LAX has a gate issue, and there are restrictions on what you can do, at least as of today. Now, if we go back to 2017, you know, this was when Delta put the grand plan in action.
transcript.zh: LAX 存在登机口紧缺的问题，至少就目前而言，你的运力布局是受限的。如果把时间倒回 2017 年，那正是达美将宏伟蓝图付诸实施的时候。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And this, all the credit in the world to Delta. They have been the most forward-thinking for the longest time.
transcript.zh: 在这件事上，达美确实值得所有赞誉。长期以来，他们的战略前瞻性一直是最强的。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And so, they looked at it and they said, "Well, our gate situation sucks." They came up with a plan, and they got a deal with LAX, with a bunch of different airlines, and they took over Terminals 2 and 3.
transcript.zh: 他们当时审视自身处境说：“我们的登机口资源太差了。”于是他们拿出了方案，与 LAX 以及多家不同航司达成了协议，直接接管了 2 号和 3 号航站楼。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Completely renovated 2, knocked down 3 and rebuilt it, which they accelerated during the pandemic, which was, again, a fantastic plan.
transcript.zh: 他们对 2 号航站楼进行了全面改造，拆除了 3 号航站楼并推倒重建，且在疫情期间加速了工程进度，这又是一次绝妙的操作。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: They put all these lounges in, they've created a space that is very welcoming to the premium Los Angeles passenger. They have 27 gates, it connects to their partners in the Bradley terminal, they are done, they have built this.
transcript.zh: 他们建了所有的贵宾休息室，打造出了一个对洛杉矶高端两舱旅客极为友好的空间。他们坐拥 27 个登机口，还能直通布拉德利航站楼的联营伙伴。他们的布局已经大功告成。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: American and United do not have that luxury at the moment.
transcript.zh: 美航和美联航目前可没有这种奢侈待遇。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: No, they don't. And if United was telling us that it wanted to fly 240 flights a day from LAX, we would know that that would be impossible because they don't have the gate space.
transcript.zh: 确实没有。如果美联航跟我们说他们想在 LAX 每天飞 240 个航班，我们都知道这绝不可能，因为他们根本没有足够的登机口机位。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: But we're talking about something very narrow here. American wants to be the global, premier US airline, emphasis for this part on "global."
transcript.zh: 但我们现在讨论的是一个非常聚焦的切口。美航想成为全美领先的全球化航司，这里我们要划重点的是“全球化”。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: So, we're really only talking about United having enough gate space to mess with American on certain transpacific flights from LAX.
transcript.zh: 所以，我们真正探讨的只是美联航是否有足够的登机口资源，在 LAX 出港的某些跨太平洋航线上阻击美航。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: And so, there tends to be a way for an airline to add four or five widebody flights per day to mess with a competitor. I suspect that United can figure that out.
transcript.zh: 通常来说，航司总能腾出办法每天加飞四五班宽体机来恶心竞争对手。我推测美联航肯定能解决这个问题。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: If we had had this conversation a year and a half ago, we would have said, "How can United fly twi—"
transcript.zh: 如果我们在一年半前聊这个话题，我们肯定会问：“美联航怎么可能飞两——”

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: to Hong Kong from LAX, the gates don't exist because United historically, or at least until it gave some gates to American, but that's another story, has not been in Terminal 6. Well, lo and behold, United found some gate space in Terminal 6 to run the Hong Kong flight. An airline can't double in size or add 30% more flights in the same number of gates. But if strategically you need four or five extra flights, you're going to figure out how to do it.
transcript.zh: 从洛杉矶飞往香港的登机口不存在，因为从历史上看，或者至少在它把一些登机口让给American之前（那是另一个故事了），United一直不在6号航站楼。但瞧瞧，United在6号航站楼找着了登机口空间来运营香港航线。一家航司不可能在相同数量的登机口下规模翻倍或增加30%的航班。但如果战略上需要多开四五班，你总能想出办法办到。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Yeah, possibly so. And really, American is coming into a very different environment than when it left. Today, between the three of them, seats to Asia are up over where they were when American was doing all this flying. Delta and United have been growing and backfilling. So when American comes into this, you now have a tougher market to go into.
transcript.zh: 是的，可能确实如此。而且说真的，American面临的竞争环境跟它离开时截然不同。如今，这三大航飞往亚洲的座位数比American以前频繁执飞时还要多。Delta和United一直在扩张并填补空缺。所以当American重新进场时，面对的是一个更严峻的市场。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Granted, before you had an American that was flying 20 premium seats on some 787s, right? Which you have very clearly told us about in the past about how this drove you insane. So now you have a more premium airline, presumably using more premium-heavy aircraft, though we don't know, because this is all still unofficial in terms of filed flights. But that means that maybe it will be better for them. But on the other hand, with United and Delta breathing down your neck, that is a tough hill to climb.
transcript.zh: 诚然，以前American在某些787上只配了20个高端舱位，对吧？你过去清清楚楚跟我们吐槽过这有多让你抓狂。所以现在他们成了定位更偏高端的航司，大概会用高端舱占比更高的飞机，虽然我们还不确定，因为航班排期申报上还没正式公布。但这意味着情况可能会有所好转。可另一方面，有United和Delta紧咬不放，这绝对是一场硬仗。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: So, look, we can go around in circles about this forever if we want, and we'll have plenty of time to do that in the coming years, I'm sure. But the reality is there is a vision at American, it has been set, and they are moving in that direction. It sounds like we have a belief, maybe, that it's the right direction in terms of going premium.
transcript.zh: 所以听着，关于这事儿我们爱怎么兜圈子讨论都行，而且我敢肯定未来几年我们有的是时间来聊。但现实是，American确实有自己的愿景，目标已经确立，他们也正朝着那个方向推进。听起来我们可能也认为，往高端化走的方向是对的。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: But is it worth it to lose so much money in LA to achieve this global part of the strategy? We don't know. We can guess about this as much as we want, but based on the history, it doesn't look great. But this is also, in theory, a different American.
transcript.zh: 但为了实现这一全球战略布局，在洛杉矶亏损那么多钱到底值不值？我们不得而知。我们大可以随便揣测，但从过往历史来看，前景并不乐观。不过从理论上讲，现在的American也今非昔比了。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Brett, that's a very diplomatic answer, but let me say something for the bulletin boards at Skyview: This is corporate suicide.
transcript.zh: Brett，这个回答非常圆滑外交，但容我对Skyview（美航总部）公告栏上的人放句狠话：这简直是自杀行为。

transcript.en: Leo Duran produced and edited this episode. Our theme music is by Joshua Mosier. Thanks for listening, and we'll be back soon.
transcript.zh: 本期节目由Leo Duran制作并剪辑。主题音乐由Joshua Mosier创作。感谢您的收听，我们很快再会。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Brian, how else am I supposed to get to Cleveland for cheap?
transcript.zh: Brian，不然我还能怎么便宜地去克利夫兰呢？

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Weren't they flying Dallas for a while, too, with like a single red-eye just to make their displeasure known about something?
transcript.zh: 他们之前不也是飞了一段时间达拉斯吗，就排了一趟红眼航班，单纯为了表达对某些事的不满？
